newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran annualized inflation slows to 17.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Iran annualized inflation slows to 17.4 pct.

text.p: Annualized inflation in Iran dropped to 17.4 percent in the four months to July 22, versus 28 percent in the same period the previous year, a newspaper said on Monday.
The daily Iran also quoted central bank figures as showing that consumer prices rose at a year-on-year rate of 18.1 percent in the month to July 22, versus 18.8 percent the previous month.
Inflation in the last Iranian year to March 20, 1997, stood at 23.2 percent against 49.4 percent the year before, according to official figures.
Economists say the government's estimate of inflation is based on official prices of a basket of commodities and goods.

In 1994 Iran set up wide-ranging price controls, but economists say most consumers are obliged to buy necessities at higher black-market prices to avoid having to queue for goods in short supply sold at official prices.
Steep price rises are a common complaint, and the government come under attack in the press and parliament for not doing enough to fight inflation.
